name: Amritsari Kulcha
subtitle: crisp-bottomed stuffed maida bread, blistered and crushed under a spoonful of butter

ingredients.note: the stuffing must be cold and dry

prepNotes: Boil the potatoes the day before if you can. Warm, freshly boiled potato steams inside the kulcha and tears it open.
The dough needs 2 hours at room temperature after kneading. Softer than chapati dough, almost sticky.
Get the oven and a heavy baking tray or upturned tawa to their maximum heat for at least 20 minutes before the first kulcha goes in.

steps.text: Mix the maida, baking soda, sugar and salt. Rub in the ghee, then work in the yogurt and enough lukewarm water to make a soft, slightly tacky dough. Knead 8 minutes until smooth.
Oil the surface of the dough, cover with a damp cloth and rest 2 hours in a warm spot. It should feel puffy and slack, not springy.
steps.tip: Under-rested dough gives you a hard flatbread rather than a kulcha.

steps.text: Grate the cold potatoes coarsely. Do not mash. Mix with the onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander leaves, anardana, amchur, chaat masala, coriander powder, crushed cumin, chilli powder and salt.
steps.tip: Grated potato keeps the filling loose. Mashed potato turns to glue and pushes through the dough.

steps.text: Divide the dough and the filling into 6 each. Flatten a dough ball in your palm, cup a portion of filling inside, gather the edges over it and pinch shut. Rest the sealed balls 10 minutes, seam down.
Roll each ball out to a 15cm oval, using dry maida, pressing outwards from the centre with even weight and stopping if the filling threatens to break through.
Press nigella seeds and a little chopped coriander into the top surface, then flip and wet the underside with water using your palm.
Slap the wet side onto the screaming-hot tray or upturned tawa. It will stick. Bake or cook 3-4 minutes until the top blisters and browns in patches.
steps.tip: The water is what makes it grip the surface, exactly like a tandoor wall. Do not skip it.

steps.text: If using a tawa, invert the tawa over the flame for 40 seconds to char the top directly.
Prise the kulcha off with a spatula, brush hard with softened butter, then crush it once between both palms so it cracks open.
steps.tip: The crush is the point. It shatters the crust and lets the butter into the filling.

steps.text: Serve immediately with pindi chole and sliced onion.

storage: Kulcha is a same-hour bread. It keeps 1 day wrapped in foil; revive on a hot tawa for 90 seconds a side with a smear of butter. The stuffing keeps 2 days refrigerated on its own.
